entries.appliesTo: nonhuman entities, including agents powered by artificial intelligence, seeking licensure or using professional titles in nursing, medicine, or as physician assistants

sources.aiPracticeRule: § 1920(h), Title 24 — 'A nonhuman entity, including an agent powered by artificial intelligence, may not be licensed in any of the following'; § 1720(k), Title 24 — 'A nonhuman entity, including an agent powered by artificial intelligence, may not be certified to practice medicine in the State.'; § 1773(d), Title 24 — 'A nonhuman entity, including an agent powered by artificial intelligence, may not be licensed as a physician assistant in the State.'
sources.scope: § 1920(h) — 'may not be licensed'; § 1720(k) — 'may not be certified to practice medicine in the State'; § 1773(d) — 'may not be licensed as a physician assistant in the State'

flags: Title-use prohibition fits no listed duty: § 1920(i) — 'A nonhuman entity, including an agent powered by artificial intelligence, may not use any of the following titles or abbreviations' (APRN, CRNA, CNS, CNP, CNM, Nurse, RN, LPN, Doctor/'Dr.'); parallel title bans in § 1720(l) (Doctor/'Dr.', Physician or surgeon, MD, DO) and § 1773(d) ('may not use the title physician assistant or the abbreviation "PA"').
No penalty or enforcement provision in this text; exposure omitted (silence is silence).
Prohibition only — bill imposes no ongoing compliance program on licensed human providers or operators; coded company because it constrains private AI products, not government or schools.
Covered professions (in appliesTo, no param slot in this family): professional nursing, APRN, practical nursing (§ 1920(h)(1)-(3)), medicine (§ 1720(k)), physician assistant (§ 1773(d)).
